name: bt5-engine-input-codes
title: Build targets stage 5: engine key, mouse-button and gamepad codes instead of GLFW's; GLFW codes translated only at the GLFW boundary
issue: User request, 2026-11-10: 'I would like for the engine to be able to allow the user to select a build target in the engine editor UI like windows, linux, android, ios, web, and maybe other console toolchains in the future like switch'. Design and stage table: orchestrator/proposals/build-targets-design.md. Stage 5 of section 5.
acceptance: InputMapping and bindings use engine codes; no GLFW constant outside the code that talks to GLFW
Saved input settings and bindings load unchanged (migration or same numeric values), with a test
Lua key names and the web input map unchanged; full engine_tests, web_tests and the web smoke pass
Saved data that holds GLFW key numbers (scenes, action maps, input settings; the key field of a binding) is migrated on load, with a test for a file saved before this stage
The editor inspector shows and edits keys by name as before
gate: needs the user's go; depends on the Triangle-Like input branches being merged to master first (feat-lua-key-text-input, feat-input-touch, feat-input-gamepad-rumble, feat-input-gamepad-composites): this stage rewrites that code
notes: Reviewer: every GLFW code has an engine code, the mapping is total both ways, saved data compatible.
